piece.caption:
How to automate customer order confirmations and form responses using Zapier and AI.

If you run an online shop or service office, checking Google Forms or store orders manually leads to delayed notifications. Connecting Zapier to your AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT lets you create automated workflows in natural language. For instance, when a buyer submits a form or places a Shopify order, Zapier can post the order details or a quick poll directly to your Telegram team chat within moments. Zapier keeps running even when your chat is closed. Remember to check your connection authorizations inside Zapier so account tokens remain secure.

Comment ZAPIER for the step-by-step setup guide.

piece.dm_text:
Here is the step-by-step workflow guide to automate Telegram notifications with Zapier:

1. Add Zapier to your AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor).
2. Connect your Telegram account and source apps (Shopify, Google Forms, or Google Sheets) inside Zapier.
3. Prompt your AI assistant with your workflow requirement (e.g., 'When a new Shopify order comes in, send an order confirmation in Telegram with the order number').
4. Your agent drafts the Zap and deploys it to Zapier.
5. Zapier runs the workflow automatically every time a new order or form entry lands, even with your laptop closed.

Source details: https://zapier.com/blog/automate-telegram

[61] Zapier Blog — How to automate Telegram with your AI agent and Zapier
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/automate-telegram
These days, more and more customers prefer to interact with businesses through messaging . If you've already invested in chat-based marketing and sales, you're probably familiar with Telegram , a popular cloud-based, encrypted instant messaging service.
But don't write it off as just another platform to keep up with. Telegram can actually be a great tool for fostering customer engagement without any extra manual work. When you pair it with Zapier, you can create entire automated Zap workflows—that power your customer interactions, sales processes, and more.
Add Zapier to your AI assistant, describe what should happen, and your agent builds the Zap. Zapier runs it from there, even once the chat is closed. (Prefer to build from a visual editor? That works too.) Here's how it works.
Build automations from wherever you work. Describe the outcome you want, and Zapier connects your tools, runs the steps, and stays on the job after you close the chat. Combine AI with reliable, deterministic automation across 10,000+ apps. Get started for free.
Build Telegram automations from your AI assistant
Telegram automations to ask your agent to build
4 ways to automate Telegram with Zap templates
Build Telegram automations from your AI assistant
Here's how a new order turns into a Telegram message without anyone typing it:
Add Zapier to your AI assistant. Add Zapier to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or whatever AI tool you use. Then connect Telegram and the apps that feed it, like Shopify, Google Forms, or Google Sheets.
Say what should happen. "When a new Shopify order comes in, send an order confirmation in Telegram with the order number."
Your agent builds the Zap. A Zap is an automated workflow that runs on its own. Your agent drafts it, deploys it to Zapier, and walks you through what it made.
Zapier takes it from there. The Zap fires the moment a new order or response arrives, and keeps firing with your laptop closed.
Zapier connects to 10,000+ apps, so Telegram can sit at the end of just about any workflow in your stack.
You can ask your AI assistant to draft a message. Zapier is what makes sure it gets sent at the right moment:
It starts when something happens. A scheduled task in an AI tool only checks for news on a timer. A Zap starts when the order or form submission lands, so the Telegram message goes out within moments.
It reaches your whole stack. Zapier connects to 10,000+ apps. Your agent can pull a new row from Google Sheets, an order from your online store, or a response from a form app, send the message through Telegram, and log the same event in your CRM.
It runs the same way every time. Every order confirmation reads the same on a quiet Tuesday as it does on Black Friday. Zaps use AI only for steps that need judgment, like summarizing a long form response before it posts, and run everything else as regular steps, which are faster and cheaper.
It fixes itself. If your Telegram connection stops working or the spreadsheet a Zap watches gets reorganized, Zapier finds the problem and proposes a fix you can approve, or applies fixes on its own if you let it.
Your agent gets access, not your keys. Zapier holds the connections to Telegram, your store, and your spreadsheets, so no bot token or store credentials get pasted into a chat. Everything you build, whichever AI tool you build it from, shows up in one place in Zapier.
Telegram automations to ask your agent to build
Once Zapier is connected, try one of these in your AI assistant:
Confirm new orders. "When a new order comes in on Shopify, send an order confirmation message in Telegram with the order number and tracking link."
Stay on top of form responses. "When someone submits my Google Form, send the answers to our team's Telegram group. If it's a feedback form, also post a poll asking the team how to respond."
Get notified about spreadsheet rows. "Whenever a new row is added to my Demo Requests sheet, message me in Telegram with the name and company."
Message from any source. "When my booking system sends a webhook for a new appointment, post the details in Telegram."
Flag only what's urgent. "Read each new form submission and decide whether it's an urgent appointment request or routine feedback. Only message the on-call chat in Telegram for the urgent ones." This is a good example of a Zap that uses AI only where judgment is needed.
4 ways to automate Telegram with Zap templates
Want to build in Zapier directly? Zap templates are pre-made Zaps you set up in Zapier itself. Clicking "Try it" opens the template in Zapier, not in your AI assistant, and you can tailor it and switch it on from there. Here are four Telegram automations as templates. If you'd rather have an agent build the Zap, use the prompts above.
To get started with a Zap template—what we call our pre-made workflows—just click on the button. It only takes a few minutes to set up. You can read more about setting up Zaps here.
When someone places an order online, letting them know you received it is a crucial part of the customer experience. With more and more people using their phones to make online purchases, it's the perfect chance to meet the customer where they are and confirm their order via text.
Of course, you can't manually send a text for every single order you receive—so automation is a great option. You can create a Zap that automatically sends a text to the customer whenever there's a new order in your eCommerce app. That way, they get instant confirmation that their purchase was successful, as well as any relevant information like the order number or tracking info.
Send messages in Telegram for new orders in Shopify
Send polls in Telegram from new Shopify orders
Send messages on Telegram for new orders in WooCommerce
Send Telegram polls for new WooCommerce orders
Send messages on Telegram for new sales in ClickBank
If you're on the go a lot, keeping on top of something as dynamic as form responses can be a challenge—especially if you use those forms to collect time-sensitive information like user feedback or appointment requests.
Instead of trying to pass every new submission on to your team manually, you can use a Zap to automatically send those responses via Telegram. This way, everyone can stay up to date on new form responses—and act accordingly.
Send messages in Telegram for new entries in Typeform
Send Telegram messages for new Webflow form submissions
If you want to work on form responses more collaboratively, you can also use a Zap to send polls in Telegram every time you receive new submissions. That way, you can quickly align with your team on the right response.
Send polls in Telegram for every new form response in Google Forms
Send polls in Telegram for new Jotform responses
Get notifications for new spreadsheet data

[62] Zapier Blog — How to orchestrate AI workflows in 4 steps with Zapier
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/ai-orchestration-workflows
Growing up as a band kid, I would have considered it the height of achievement to someday conduct a symphonic orchestra. (What can I say—I was really cool and popular as a teenager.) As an adult tech writer (equally as cool), workflow orchestration is the next best thing. It's slightly less glamorous, but it still lets me live out my control-freak dreams—this time with triggers, filters, and AI steps instead of French horns.
It's easy for your team's AI experiments to feel more like a messy jam session than a polished performance. You'll often end up with scattered tools, inconsistent logic, and rogue automations duct-taped together behind the scenes.
You can bring order to the chaos with Zapier. Tell your AI assistant what should happen, and Zapier keeps it running long after the chat closes. Or build it directly in Zapier, if that's where you're most comfortable. And since Zapier connects 10,000+ apps, your setup can work across your entire stack.
In this guide, I'll give you a repeatable, 4-step framework that helps your team orchestrate smarter systems.
The 4-step framework to orchestrate AI workflows
Common AI orchestration pitfalls and how to avoid them
AI orchestration is the end-to-end coordination of data, tools, and AI models so each step of a business process triggers the next without human hand-offs.
When done right, AI orchestration helps businesses move from fragmented, one-off AI experiments to fully integrated, intelligent workflows. It connects every part of your AI pipeline—tools, data, models, and human decision points—into a seamless system. That means fewer manual steps, tighter alignment across teams, and faster, more scalable outcomes.
How orchestration differs from automation and integration
Terms like integration , automation , and orchestration often get used interchangeably. While they're related, they solve different problems. Here's a quick breakdown:
Connecting a form builder to your CRM (or connecting those accounts with Zapier , if they don't have a built-in integration with each other)
Runs predefined rules to act on that data automatically
Triggering a Slack alert when a deal closes in your CRM
Coordinates entire processes across tools and logic layers
Qualifying a lead, enriching it with AI, and routing it to a salesperson based on region and score
Orchestration is like the final boss of digital optimization for your business. And unlike traditional workflow orchestration , which often follows rigid rule-based paths, AI orchestration introduces dynamic logic and adaptive behavior. It lets systems decide what to do next based on real-time inputs—like sentiment, context, or historical performance.
And the best part (at least to my very right-brained mind) is that you don't need an engineering background. With Zapier, anyone on your team can design and deploy orchestrated AI workflows by describing them to an AI tool or building them in the visual editor—turning complex logic into systems that are fast to build and easy to update.
Want to dive deeper into the differences between integration, automation, and orchestration? Check out our full guide to AI orchestration .
How to know if your team is ready for orchestration
AI orchestration isn't just for massive enterprises with teams of data scientists. If you're already automating parts of your workflow—or if your team's operations feel fragmented and reactive—you may be more ready than you think.
Here are a few signs it's time to take the next step:
Manual hand-offs are slowing things down. You rely on humans to move data from one tool to another, which creates delays, errors, and missed opportunities.
You're running 50+ Zaps—and it's getting hard to track. You've automated plenty of tasks, but you lack a centralized view of how they all connect.
You want smarter workflows, not just faster ones. Your team needs logic that adapts based on context (like customer sentiment or lead quality), not just rigid if-this-then-that flows.
You're already enriching data with AI, but results live in silos. Tools like ChatGPT , Claude , or Gemini are part of your stack, but their outputs aren't feeding into broader business processes.
Cross-functional collaboration is stalling. Marketing, Sales, IT, or Ops are building their own workflows without visibility into how each other's systems work.
If any of these sound familiar, orchestration can be your next step. A good first move is to list the Zaps you already run and sketch how they connect, so you can see where the gaps and overlaps are before building anything new.
The 4-step framework to orchestrate AI workflows
Zapier brings together 10,000+ apps and enterprise-level guardrails in one place. It gives you the power to orchestrate AI across your tech stack with flexibility and control, no matter your team or department.
Install Zapier in your AI assistant, describe what should happen, and your agent drafts the Zap and deploys it to Zapier. (You can also build the same Zap directly in Zapier, whichever you prefer.) From there, Zapier starts it when something happens in your apps, or on a schedule, and runs it the same way every time. Every run is logged, and if something breaks, Zapier proposes a fix.
And because no one wants to babysit rogue automations, Zapier bakes in governance from the start: version history, execution logs, and built-in error handling (like retries or real-time Slack alerts). These are the kinds of guardrails that keep things safe, compliant, and scalable.
2. Add logic and intelligence with paths, filters, formatters, and AI steps
You can chat with your agent (or Zapier Copilot) to refine your automations as needed: add new triggers or steps, modify field mappings, insert conditional logic, or swap underlying apps—all via further prompts. You can also add AI by Zapier steps (with access to 40+ AI models) to integrate LLMs directly into your automated workflows.
Here's an example of what that might end up looking like:
Trigger: "New support ticket in Freshdesk"
Filter: "Only continue if email field is filled out"
Format: "Clean up ticket text" (strip signatures, normalize formatting)
AI step: "Summarize the issue using ChatGPT" or "Suggest a likely root cause"
Path step: " Route urgent tickets to the on-call engineer in Slack, and send other incidents to Jira"
In this example, AI orchestration lets you create a smart chain that adapts based on the ticket's content and urgency. You'll end up with fewer bottlenecks, faster responses, and a helpdesk that feels less like a queue and more like a concierge.
3. Set guardrails: error handling and human review
The more powerful your orchestration becomes, the more important guardrails are. Here are four ways to stay in control:
Human-in-the-loop steps : Route sensitive outputs (e.g., legal copy) to humans for sign-off.
Multi-path error logic : Retry failures or add error handling settings (like sending alerts via Slack).
